subject: Nexa Bank - Private Offer MAP & procurement milestones
messages:
From: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@nexabank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nexabank.com, rajiv.menon@nexabank.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — procurement path and timeline

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to get back with the specific steps we need to get a private offer set up through AWS Marketplace (we prefer private offers for centralized billing). Can you send a mutual action plan (MAP) that includes:
- Exact artifacts procurement needs to approve (SOW, SKUs, pricing sheet)
- Who at Redwood will be the point for contract and marketplace setup
- Typical timelines for private offer creation, approval, and first invoice
- Any pre-reqs (SOC2 evidence, commercial terms, billing contact fields)

We aim to have procurement sign off in the next 3 weeks if possible.

Best,
Aditi
Senior Platform PM, Nexa Bank

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@nexabank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation — procurement path and timeline

Hi Aditi —

Appreciate the clear ask. I attached a first-pass MAP (NexaBank_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short SOW draft. High level answers below, then a suggested milestone plan.

Key contacts at Redwood:
- Marketplace/setup & billing: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwood.com)
- Legal & contract redlines: Neha Kapoor (neha.kapoor@redwood.com)
- Solutions / onboarding: me (vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com)

Procurement artifacts we typically provide:
- Pricing worksheet (SKU mapping + list price and committed monthly units)
- Private Offer request doc (for AWS/GCP/Azure marketplaces)
- Draft MSA / SOW (we can accept customer PO after signature depending on deal flow)
- SOC 2 Type II report + penetration test summary (we can provide via secure share)

Timelines (typical):
1) MAP & pricing agreed (3–5 business days once we have final SKUs)
2) Private offer creation by Redwood + marketplace submission (1–3 business days)
3) Marketplace approval (AWS: 2–7 business days typical; can be expedited with reseller code)
4) Invoice start / billing cycle: first invoice issued once private offer is live and initial usage is recorded; we can align invoice to your billing cadence.

Suggested three-week milestone plan (high level):
- Week 1: Confirm SKUs and pricing, procurement reviews SOW
- Week 2: Redwood submits private offer to AWS marketplace; procurement completes internal approvals
- Week 3: Marketplace approval and first invoice / PO issued

I've flagged a few questions in the MAP about billing contact fields and whether Nexa needs consolidated invoicing vs. direct AWS billing. Can your procurement contact reply to the flagged cells in the spreadsheet?

Thanks — Karthik will coordinate the marketplace submission once we have the signed MAP.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: NexaBank_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 sheets)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Nexa Bank MAP questions / AWS private offer notes

Team — quick internal thread to line up roles. Notes from my side:
- For AWS private offers we need: SKUs, list price, committed units (if reserved), and a billing contact email (used to map invoices).
- If Nexa wants Redwood to own the metering and invoice, we must set up consolidated billing via Marketplace Metering Service (we've done this for other banks).
- AWS approval can be delayed if procurement wants custom legal terms in the Offer; recommend we accept standard marketplace purchase terms and handle contractual changes via separate MSA. That shortens the marketplace window.

Action items I propose:
1) Vanessa: get procurement to confirm consolidated invoicing vs. direct customer billing (fill MAP)
2) Neha: prepare a redline-friendly MSA + SOW (send to Aditi)
3) Markus: stand by for SOC2 secure share link once procurement requests evidence

I'll prepare the private offer package template and submit once we have sign-off on pricing.

-Karthik
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@nexabank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, rajiv.menon@nexabank.com
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Nexa Bank MAP v1 — requested answers and timeline (please review)

Hi Aditi / Rajiv —

Following up with the MAP and a compact milestone table. I've filled the billing/contact fields we discussed; please confirm the selections in the attached spreadsheet. Key points:
- Redwood can accept consolidated invoicing via AWS marketplace (Redwood invoices Nexa monthly) — we marked that as our recommendation to align with your finance ops.
- If Nexa prefers direct AWS billing, that adds an extra step for your Procurement to enable marketplace billing.
- We can submit the private offer to AWS once pricing and billing contact are final.

Milestone table (high level):
- 24 Mar: MAP reviewed and returned with billing preference + PO/contract owner
- 25–26 Mar: Redwood prepares private offer + uploads to AWS marketplace
- 29–31 Mar: AWS review window (expedite possible)
- 1 Apr: Private offer expected live / first usage billing window (contingent on approvals)

Attachments included: NexaBank_MAP_v1.xlsx, Redwood_SOW-draft.pdf

Please let me know if procurement needs a consolidated pricing sheet in CSV format for your systems — we can provide that.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@nexabank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@nexabank.com>
Cc: procurement@nexabank.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 13:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nexa Bank MAP v1 — requested answers and timeline (please review)

Vanessa — thanks for the clear plan. Procurement reviewed the MAP and confirmed: consolidated invoicing via Redwood is preferred. We've attached our standard PO template (see procurement@nexabank.com for upload).

Next asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a DocuSign link for the SOW + MSA redline acceptance?
- Please include a clear SKU-to-aws-product-code mapping in the private offer payload so our finance team can ingest charges cleanly.

If you can get the private offer submitted by EOD 26 Mar we will route internal approvals quickly.

Regards,
Rajiv
Director, Procurement, Nexa Bank
